main_text.head: HYPOMNEMATA IN HABACVC PROPHETAM.
main_text.p: Lectio i. Augustini ii [?] 1581.CUM in hac tanta Ecclesiæ mi-litantis, & laboribus senió-que iam confectæ afflictio-ne & mœsticia, Pijs omnib: capita attollenda, & iam in-stans redemptio expectanda sit: plurimum nostra interest, habere in conspectu aliquot grauissima selectissimaq; Patrū dicta, quæ monent, fatalem esse Ecclesiæ Christi crucem, & eam maximum habe-re usum, ac proinde nemini pio defugi-endam.
Ecclesia, ut inquit Augustinus, velut li-lium inter spinas, malis & bonis est per-mixta. Quis igitur miretur se pungi rerum molestisimarum sensu?
Gregorius, Ecclesiam, inquit, Christus crucis suæ hæredem constituit. Quis nostrum igitur eam detrectet defugiatq;?
Sed & hoc memoria dignisimum est, quod coronidis vice ex diui Hilarij li.7. de Trinitate, ideo adducemus, quia mo-net; veram Ecclesiam propter veritatis

page.notes: Marginal note at upper right reads "Lectio i." then "Augustini" with a numeral that looks like "ii" (uncertain) and "1581." Page number at head is a small mark that could be "1" or "i" (uncertain). Show-through from the reverse side is visible at the top and in the right margin and was omitted. Original spelling kept, including "dignisimum", "molestisimarum", "mœsticia" and "omnib:". The large initial C is a woodcut, read as CUM. The word "pungi" is as printed.
